farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾.
This is the first of the Qur'an that was revealed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him.

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ﴾.
It was said «من علق», whereas it is [one] «علقةٌ» (clot), because «الإنسان» has a plural meaning; so «العلق» was taken as plural, to match the verse-endings.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ﴾.
He did not say: أن رأى نفسه (that he saw himself). When the Arabs make a verb that is satisfied with one noun [i.e. a verb with a single object] fall upon themselves, or make it fall from someone else upon himself, they put «نفس» in the place of the pronoun. So they say: قتلتَ نفسك (you killed yourself), and they do not say: قتلتَك or قتلته [for the same person]; and they say: قتل نفسَه (he killed himself) and قتلتُ نفسى (I killed myself). But when the verb requires a noun and a predicate (khabar), they drop «النفس» and say: متى تراك خارجاً (when do you consider yourself going out?) and متى نظنك خارجاً (when do we think you are going out?). [Translator's note: «نظنك» is as printed; the parallel with «تراك» suggests «تظنك» (when do you think yourself …).] And His word, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ﴾, is of this kind.

farraa:9-10.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ (9) عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ﴾.
It was revealed concerning Abū Jahl: he used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at his place of prayer, and harm him and forbid him; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ﴾?, meaning the Prophet ﷺ.

farraa:13-13.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾.
There is an Arabic [construction] in it. Its like in ordinary speech would be if it were said: أرأيت الذى ينهى عبداً إذا صلّى وهو كاذب متولٍّ عن الذكر؟ (Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays, while he is lying and turning away from the Reminder?), i.e.: what could be more astonishing than this?

farraa:14-14.t:
Then He said — woe to him! — ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ﴾.
Meaning Abū Jahl. Then He said: ﴿كَلاَّ لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ﴾.
His forelock (ناصيته): the front of his head; i.e.: We shall surely bend it down, We shall surely seize it, We shall surely abase him and humiliate him. It is also said: We shall surely drag [him] by the forelock to the Fire, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِى والأَقْدَامِ﴾, and they are thrown into the Fire. It is also said: We shall surely blacken his face; so the forelock stood in for the face, because it is at the front of the face.

farraa:15-16.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ نَاصِيَةٍ﴾.
By repetition (takrīr, i.e. badal (substitute)), as He said: ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ، صِرَاطِ اللهِ﴾. The definite is made to follow the indefinite by repetition, and the indefinite the definite. Whoever puts (ناصيةً) in the accusative makes it an act of the definite [Translator's note: so the source, «جعله فعلا للمعرفة»; the sense appears to be that the accusative is governed with reference to the definite «الناصية», e.g. as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the wording may be corrupt], and it is permissible in reading.

farraa:17-18.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾.
They are stronger, and they work with hands and feet; and the she-camel تزْبِن (pushes off) the milker and kicks him with her foot.
Al-Kisāʾī said, later in life: the singular of «الزبانية» is زِبْنِىٌّ; before that he used to say: I have not heard a singular for it. And I do not know whether it was by analogy (qiyās) on his part or by hearing (samāʿ). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "كَلاَّ لئِن لَّمْ يَنْتَهِ لأسْفَعاً بِالنَّاصِيَةِ", and in it also: "فَلْيَدْعُ إلىّ نَادِيَه فَسَأَدْعُو الزَّبَانِيَة".
